newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bamerindus' Euronotes a Bear Stearns buy.
newsitem.headline: Bamerindus' Euronotes a Bear Stearns buy.

text.p: Bear Stearns said it recommends purchase of Bamerindus' outstanding Euronotes maturing in June 31 1997, Oct 6, 1997 and Oct 29 1998.
The brokerage said in a report that, at 531 basis points (bps), 541 bps and 611 bps, respectively, the Euronotes offer above market spreads for risk-oriented investors.
"Although Bamerindus' precarious financial situation is well known, the market has not adequately considered the Brazilian government's implied support for the bank," the report said.

Bamerindus, Brazil's fourth-largest private bank, has been forced to restructure and seek alternatives including a Central Bank loan to overcome liquidity troubles, which fueled speculation that the bank would be sold.
Bear Stearns noted resolutions of previous Brazilian-bank failures contribute to its view that Bamerindus is a likely acquisition or merger target.
"As such, we believe spreads on these bonds could narrow approximately 200 bps before year end," it added.

The brokerage also noted Bamerindus is Brazil's largest financier of foreign trade and the second largest lender to the agriculture sector. Among private Brazilian banks, it ranks fourth in assets, totalling 20 billion reais, meaning the bank "is too big to fail."
"The bank's possible failure represents an enormous risk to the Brazilian financial system that the government does not ignore," the report said.
